text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: service /v1/generate p99 latency > 6s in us-east-1. Impact: degraded response times for hosted customers. Trigger: autoscaler throttles. thread created 3899123456
Anya (primary): I'm on it. switching primary->secondary handover in 2m if I need help. anyone seeing errors beyond latency?
Matt (infra): seeing increased queue length on gen-queue-1, some containers reporting OOMs. digging into kube events.
Liz (sre): tagging runbooks: https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/latency-p99 and https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/k8s-oom-restart — start there.
Ben (ops): confirmed spike correlates with model-x rollout at 03:08 UTC. We should consider immediate rollback to model-x-v2 -> model-x-v1.
Anya (primary): good catch. can we do an emergency rollback? deploy-bot, status?
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline for model-x rollbacks show: canary health failing -> rollback available. Run `./scripts/rollback_model.sh model-x-v1` to start.
Matt (infra): before rolling back, quick mitigation: scale gen-pool from 8 -> 12 for us-east-1 to buy time. `kubectl scale deployment gen-pool --replicas=12 -n prod-us-east`
Anya (primary): doing scale now. will watch p99. if no improvement in 90s, perform rollback.
Liz (sre): check cache KV-hit ratios too (`redis-kv`), sometimes new model increases prefix miss rate. `redis-cli info keyspace` and look at `used_memory` and `keyspace_hits`
Ben (ops): I've queued rollback with deploy-bot but holding until we confirm scale effect. informing SOC and CS: "investigating latency; temporary scaling in progress; rollback ready"
Anya (primary): scale applied. p99 dropping to ~4.8s -> still high but better. keep monitoring.
Matt (infra): logs show OOM killers on nodes node-ue-3 and node-ue-5. increasing node autoscaler min size by 2 as well. `gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize ...`
Liz (sre): propagation note: if nodes are under memory pressure, pods may get stuck in Pending -> try `kubectl get pods -n prod-us-east | grep CrashLoopBackOff` and restart affected pods: `kubectl rollout restart deployment gen-worker -n prod-us-east`
Anya (primary): I'm leaning to hold off on rollback for now since scaling helped. flagging action items on handoff: 1) keep autoscaler bumped until 04:30 UTC, 2) watch for OOM on any new nodes, 3) if p99 >6s again, do rollback.
Ben (ops): CS updated: "we've applied temporary capacity and monitoring; if performance doesn't improve we'll revert to previous model in under 10 minutes" :white_check_mark:
Matt (infra): restarted 3 gen-worker pods (one per affected node). memory pressure eased. p99 ~3.2s now.
Anya (primary): good. adding quick remediation checklist to thread for whoever picks up next shift: - check incident-bot alerts for /v1/generate - verify gen-pool replicas >=12 - verify node group size >= min+2 - check redis KV hit ratio and evictions - if OOM persists -> `kubectl rollout restart deployment gen-worker` - rollback command: `./scripts/rollback_model.sh model-x-v1` - contact CS with templated message (link below)
Liz (sre): runbook link for rollback + postmortem checklist: https://wiki.redwood/internal/playbooks/model-rollbacks. Also note: capture sample traces for any failed requests: `curl -X GET \"https://tracing.redwood/internal/trace?service=gen&start=...\"`
Anya (primary): leaving handoff notes for next oncall (I'm off in 25m): current state = stable, p99 ~3s, replicas 12, node autoscaler +2, rollback staged but not executed. Please escalate to prod oncall if p99 rises above 5s or error-rate >1%.
Ben (ops): I'll be secondary for the next 40m, ping me @ben if anything spikes.
Matt (infra): I'll keep watch on node scaling events and OOM logs. leaving commands in case of recurrence: `kubectl top nodes`, `kubectl describe pod <pod>` and `journalctl -u kubelet`
deploy-bot: deploy rollback job cancelled (hold). Reminder: automated canary rollback is enabled for this model.
Anya (primary): thanks team. handoff summary for next oncall in thread body above + links: latency runbook, k8s oom runbook, rollback script, CS template https://wiki.redwood/internal/templates/cs-latency-incident.
Liz (sre): small followup: open a quick ticket to track root cause with SLO regression tag. I'll create it and attach traces/logs.
Anya (primary): created ticket INC-2026-487 (root-cause tracking). attaching stack traces now. handing off to Ben.
Ben (ops): taking point. thumbs up. :thumbsup:
